relevance.rationale: Identity confirmed from the document's own cover page (Annales de l'institut Fourier, on q-summation and confluence, two authors, tome 59 no. 1 (2009) p. 347-392, item id AIF_2009__59_1_347_0 matching the filename) and matches the seeded key exactly, including volume, issue and page range. Two citation sites, both in Lean docstrings rather than at a formalised statement: QOU/Archimedean/BalancedKernelConfluence.lean:69 and :76 name it as 'the q -> 1 confluence route outside RSZ', and QOU/MathlibExt/FrechetShohat.lean:67 mentions it in passing. Not load-bearing: the citing file's actual proof legs are classical (Frechet-Shohat, Simon, Billingsley Thm 30.2 are the named inputs), and the file is explicit that what remains open is the substrate's own moment/positivity content ('at q != 1 the fibre problem is indeterminate, §3.1, so this needs derivation input beyond moments'). So the reference is signposting an alternative route, not supplying a step. Supporting: correct, in-scope, honestly used, but nothing is derived from it. Note the file's honest self-assessment is a good example of the (a)-scope discipline — it names the gap rather than papering over it with the citation.

proposedActions.rationale: Used as an explicitly-labelled alternative-route signpost in a file that is candid about its remaining gap. Promoting it to a load-bearing citation would require actually running the confluence argument, which the file says it has not.
